sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment or emotional tone the author expresses in the text (tweet-style posts, possibly in any language). Focus on the author's own feelings, attitude, or evaluation, including excitement, praise, complaints, frustration, or mockery, rather than on the topic itself.

criteria.positive: The author conveys a favourable feeling: excitement, anticipation, enjoyment, praise, pride, congratulations, hope, or celebration of an achievement or upcoming event. Light humour or casual mentions of looking forward to something count as positive, even with mild profanity.
criteria.neutral: The text mainly states facts, news, schedules, scores, announcements, offers (e.g., selling tickets), questions, or observations without a clear emotional stance from the author, or with mixed or ambiguous feelings that do not lean clearly either way.
criteria.negative: The author conveys an unfavourable feeling: complaints, frustration, disappointment, anger, sadness, fear, insults, sarcasm, criticism, or ridicule of people, products, or events. Reports of bad news, failures, or unpleasant experiences also count as negative.
